idea: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport cost between two probability distributions; in one dimension the Wasserstein-1 distance equals the integral of |F1(x)-F2(x)| between the two CDFs, and Wasserstein-p uses sorted quantiles.
does: Compare a simulated travel-time, headway, speed or daily-profile distribution with an observed or baseline one by one number (sorted-sample Wasserstein), usable as a calibration objective alongside count error and in experiment reports.
outputs: W1 distance in the original unit, quantile gaps
existing: none (stats.py has t-tests; calibration uses counts)
notes: The book is measure-theoretic stochastic control; only the 1-D distance is usable. Stdlib sort-based, a few lines.
